tasks.short: Create a content strategy from audience needs, search evidence, business priorities and publishing capacity.

steps.what: Gather search performance, campaign results and business priorities.
Audit existing content against audience needs and search coverage.

loop.input: Approved page text, content inventory, intent profiles and performance baseline.
loop.output: Proposed coverage labels and gaps, linked to source pages and intent evidence.
loop.check: Validate page identifiers and citations; the strategist reviews uncertain labels and a sample of others.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction pass per page; unresolved pages enter a review queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metrics reveal weak performance, but semantic coverage requires reading page text.

steps.what: Draft audience themes, content formats, distribution choices and success measures.

loop.input: Reviewed gaps, approved priorities, publishing capacity and brand guidelines.
loop.output: A strategy draft with source-linked themes, proposed formats, dependencies and measures.
loop.check: Check required sections, source links and capacity totals; the strategist reviews claims and coherence.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence remains explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure but cannot synthesize varied audience evidence into a coherent narrative.

steps.what: Choose priorities and trade off search demand, differentiation and production capacity.
Approve strategic priorities, capacity commitments and success measures.
Translate approved priorities into briefs, owners and a publishing schedule.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} joins search analytics from {OTHER}, campaign results from {ADS} and the content inventory from {CMS}. Bounded loops draft a coverage assessment and strategy in {DOCS}; people choose priorities and approve commitments. Configured flows create briefs and schedules in {PROJECT} from the approved strategy.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sits across systems, content meaning is hard to encode, and strategic choices have weak fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort to build connectors and document generators. Bounded text models can propose semantic coverage labels and drafts from approved sources.
tasks.still_hard: Search demand does not establish business value. Differentiation, credible expertise and production capacity still constrain the strategy.
tasks.human_edge: Choose an editorial position worth defending and reject attractive traffic that does not serve the audience or business.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on which emerging search theme deserves the next available content slot.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling evidence and formatting plans toward editorial choices and testing assumptions. Formal decision rights do not change; the marketing manager retains capacity and budget approval.

reach.task: Turn a selected search theme into an editorial brief with acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Editorial standards, source quality, commissioning and realistic production effort.

evidence.claim: Joining performance data and generating structured briefs are plausible deterministic builds; these are not documented marketing outcomes in the digest.
The digest documents product-description drafting, supporting a narrow writing capability rather than autonomous content strategy.
Strategic differentiation and capacity trade-offs still require accountable human judgement.

assumptions: This describes an internal marketing team with shared publishing capacity and periodic management approval.
The {OTHER} slot represents search analytics and keyword research tools.
The approved strategy contains structured priorities, owners, capacity limits and measures for deterministic brief creation.
Build ranges are estimates for one business unit and a small set of sources.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties are assessed for the actual data and intended use.
The design uses aggregate audience evidence, without employee monitoring; consultation under national rules is assessed if that scope changes.
unknowns: Which search analytics exports or interfaces are available and licensed.
Whether content identifiers match across {CMS}, analytics and planning records.
Who approves editorial priorities, publication and capacity commitments.
Whether intent profiles, brand guidelines and publishing capacity are maintained.
research_questions: How accurately can semantic coverage labels distinguish a passing mention from a useful answer?
Does the proposed prioritisation improve qualified engagement when evaluated against a baseline?
new_work: Review unsupported claims, uncertain coverage labels and proposed themes.
Maintain source mappings, brief templates and evaluation examples.
Investigate stale performance data and failed imports.
Compare strategy assumptions with later audience and commercial outcomes.

tasks.short: Combine keyword evidence and secondary research into useful, source-linked audience intent profiles.

steps.what: Export keyword and query evidence from search analytics tools in {OTHER} and {ADS}.
Collect relevant market studies, customer research and aggregate customer questions.
Normalise terms, remove duplicates and align geography, dates and measurement definitions.
Group queries and interpret intent using supporting secondary evidence.

loop.input: Queries, approved secondary text, source metadata and an intent taxonomy.
loop.output: Proposed query clusters and intent profiles with evidence links and uncertainty labels.
loop.check: Validate source references and numeric fields; review mixed-intent clusters and stratified samples.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass per batch; ambiguous clusters remain unclassified.
loop.why_not_simpler: Literal term rules miss paraphrases and cannot reliably connect queries with contextual research.

steps.what: Validate audience interpretations and distinguish supported needs from research hypotheses.
Share accepted profiles and link them to content and campaign planning.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects approved keyword exports from {OTHER} and {ADS}, plus research from {DOCS} and aggregate customer evidence. Deterministic checks align definitions and flag incompatible sources before a bounded loop proposes evidence-linked intent profiles. The strategist accepts interpretations, and configured notifications connect them to planning in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources use different dates, geographies and definitions. Semantic interpretation and source reliability resist simple joins.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes source adapters and validation rules cheaper to build. Bounded classification can connect paraphrased queries with approved research text.
tasks.still_hard: Search volume is not a direct measure of need, and secondary research may represent a different population. Missing or biased evidence cannot be repaired by fluent synthesis.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparent intent is an artefact of measurement, language or an unrepresentative sample.

ambition.what: Provide source-linked intent briefs for low-volume language segments previously excluded from routine research.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time aligning exports and more time resolving contradictory evidence and designing validation research. Decision rights do not change; accepted profiles remain research inputs rather than automatic campaign instructions.

reach.task: Design a small study to test an uncertain search-intent hypothesis.
reach.learn: Sampling, question design, research ethics and limits on generalising findings.

evidence.claim: Normalisation, deduplication and source lineage can be implemented deterministically when source definitions are explicit.
Bounded semantic classification can propose intent clusters, but marketing-specific accuracy needs local evaluation.
The digest provides no direct case demonstrating automated search-intent profiling.

assumptions: The {OTHER} slot represents search analytics and keyword research tools.
Secondary collection starts from an approved source register; source selection remains reviewable.
Source permissions allow this use, and personal customer details are removed before semantic processing.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply to the intended processing; this is aggregate audience research.
Employee consultation under national rules is assessed if the scope expands to staff monitoring.
Build ranges cover one source bundle and an initial set of languages; they are estimates.
unknowns: Which research licences permit extraction, processing and internal redistribution.
Which source definitions, country filters and reporting windows are available.
Whether customer questions contain personal data or confidential material.
Which languages and customer segments need coverage.
Whether a maintained intent taxonomy and labelled examples exist.
research_questions: How does model agreement vary across languages, query lengths and mixed-intent queries?
Which secondary sources add predictive value beyond keyword evidence alone?
How should uncertainty be shown so planners avoid treating hypotheses as facts?
new_work: Resolve incompatible definitions and data quality exceptions.
Review ambiguous clusters and refresh labelled evaluation samples.
Maintain source licences, provenance, retention rules and connector mappings.
Test whether accepted intent profiles predict observed audience behaviour.

tasks.short: Coordinate search marketing with other channels, agree trade-offs and record shared commitments.

steps.what: Review channel plans, campaign calendars and resource commitments.
Ask channel owners for missing dates, status and dependencies.
Prepare an alignment brief showing overlaps, gaps and competing requests.

loop.input: Current channel records, deterministic scheduling conflicts and approved business priorities.
loop.output: An alignment brief with linked dependencies, possible message conflicts and discussion questions.
loop.check: Calculate dates and capacity conflicts with code; verify record links and review semantic conflict claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per planning cycle; unresolved conflicts go to the meeting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Date rules identify collisions, but free-text plans can contradict each other without sharing dates.

steps.what: Discuss channel interactions and negotiate timing, messaging and resource trade-offs.
Approve cross-channel priorities and resolve escalated resource conflicts.
Record agreed owners, dates and dependencies, then notify channel teams.

tasks.design: A shared planning record in {PROJECT} replaces repeated status requests, with an integration showing channel schedules from {ADS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}. Deterministic checks flag scheduling conflicts, and a bounded loop drafts a source-linked alignment brief in {DOCS}. People negotiate and approve commitments; configured flows update records and notify owners through {CHAT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Channel plans use inconsistent fields, and much of the important context sits in conversations. Software can expose conflicts but cannot confer agreement.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of connecting channel records. A bounded drafting loop can turn existing context into a useful meeting brief.
tasks.still_hard: Shared records depend on timely updates. Incentives, budget competition and disagreements about attribution still need human negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, surface unspoken constraints and secure commitments that other teams will honour.

ambition.what: A weekly cross-channel sequencing decision for campaigns that compete for the same audience.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends less time chasing updates and writing recaps, leaving more time for resolving channel conflicts. Decision rights do not change; channel owners retain execution authority and the marketing manager resolves escalations.

reach.task: Coordinate a shared campaign calendar and propose a media sequencing change.
reach.learn: Media planning, channel lead times, budget commitments and attribution limitations.

evidence.claim: Shared structured records and configured notifications can replace repeated requests for dates and status when teams maintain those records.
Deterministic scheduling checks and bounded brief drafting can support coordination without automating negotiation.
The digest contains no direct case establishing automated cross-channel agreement or resource negotiation.

assumptions: Channel owners maintain dates, status and dependencies in the shared record; otherwise status chasing cannot disappear.
Approval uses structured decision fields so recording commitments does not need another text model.
The integration changes planning records, not live campaign budgets or audience settings.
Private conversations and meeting recordings are outside scope.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties are assessed for the actual processing.
Employee consultation under national rules is assessed if staff activity monitoring is introduced.
Build ranges are estimates for a small number of channel integrations.
unknowns: Whether channel teams will adopt a common planning record.
Which channel schedules and resource fields can be read through available interfaces.
Who may commit shared capacity or move campaign dates.
Which planning information requires restricted access.
research_questions: Which structured fields catch meaningful channel conflicts without creating excessive alerts?
Does an alignment brief shorten coordination time while preserving participation and commitment?
new_work: Maintain planning fields, dependency rules and access permissions.
Resolve stale records and unmatched campaign identifiers.
Review speculative message conflicts before discussion.
Check that approved commitments were recorded accurately.

tasks.short: Improve website and shopping-cart conversion through measured experiments against agreed business and customer guardrails.

steps.what: Review funnel performance, checkout outcomes and agreed KPIs.
Reconcile tracking, segment definitions and order totals before comparing conversion rates.
Inspect funnel losses and customer feedback to identify possible conversion barriers.

loop.input: Aggregate funnel losses and redacted customer feedback, linked to affected pages.
loop.output: Barrier categories and testable hypotheses with supporting evidence and uncertainty.
loop.check: Verify evidence links and counts; the strategist checks that correlation is not presented as causation.
loop.stop: One categorisation pass and one correction pass per batch; unsupported hypotheses remain flagged.
loop.why_not_simpler: Funnel rules locate losses, but interpreting varied customer explanations requires reading free text.

steps.what: Choose an experiment and specify metrics, audience, guardrails and stopping rules.
Build experiment variants in {CMS} or {ECOMMERCE} staging.
Check tracking, accessibility, mobile behaviour and checkout completion in staging.
Launch the experiment with approved audience limits and guardrails.
Calculate experiment effects, uncertainty and guardrail outcomes.
Interpret results and recommend rollout, revision or rejection.
Apply the approved rollout or restore the original experience.

tasks.design: Configured dashboards in {BI} and an experimentation system in {OTHER} use validated conversion and order data, with deterministic reconciliation on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded loop groups redacted feedback into hypotheses, while people choose experiments and review configured variants in {CMS} or {ECOMMERCE}. Deterministic QA and predefined statistical rules support manager-approved launches and releases, with automatic guardrail stops within the approved experiment limits.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tracking and order data disagree, experiments need scarce design capacity, and low traffic makes results uncertain. Repeated manual reconciliation delays learning.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes validation jobs and automated checks cheaper. Existing experiment configuration handles assignment and analysis, while a bounded loop reduces feedback-reading effort.
tasks.still_hard: Automation cannot create statistical power or establish causality from observational funnels. Checkout restrictions, consent-related missing data and long-term customer effects remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a meaningful customer problem and reject conversion gains that damage clarity, trust, accessibility or commercial quality.

ambition.what: A conversion experiment service for regional landing pages previously below the team's capacity threshold.

tasks.altitude: The strategist spends more time selecting hypotheses and interpreting evidence, with less reconciliation and experiment administration. Formal release and budget rights do not change; the marketing manager approves customer-facing changes.

reach.task: Specify an accessible checkout variant with measurable acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Interaction design, keyboard and mobile behaviour, component constraints and usability testing.

reach.task: Assess an experiment's effect on completed orders, margin and returns.
reach.learn: Order economics, payment failures, fulfilment constraints and delayed commercial outcomes.

evidence.claim: Configured experimentation can handle assignment and statistical reporting when instrumentation and stopping rules are valid.
Reconciliation and repeatable checkout checks are deterministic work; qualitative feedback interpretation can use a bounded text loop.
The digest contains no direct conversion-optimisation case or documented conversion uplift supporting this design.

assumptions: The {OTHER} slot covers web analytics, experimentation and browser testing tools, distinguished by each step's purpose.
Initial variants use existing editable templates and components; bespoke checkout engineering requires separate estimates.
The current experimentation capability supports valid assignment, predefined analysis and guardrail stops.
Traffic is sufficient for the selected experiment; inconclusive results do not trigger automatic rollout.
Customer feedback is redacted, and tracking uses an assessed lawful basis and applicable consent requirements.
GDPR and applicable EU AI Act duties apply; the intended use is ordinary website experimentation.
Consultation under national rules is assessed if the implementation adds employee monitoring.
Build ranges are estimates for one site and one checkout implementation.
unknowns: Which checkout elements can be edited and released without bespoke development.
Whether assignment, consent state and completed orders can be reconciled reliably.
Which experimentation and testing capabilities are already available.
What traffic, baseline rates and practical effect sizes support a feasible experiment.
Who may approve launches, releases and emergency restoration.
Whether existing tracking permissions cover the proposed experimentation.
research_questions: Which reconciliation checks best distinguish instrumentation failures from real funnel changes?
What experiment design remains valid under sparse traffic and consent-related missingness?
Which guardrails capture harmful effects on accessibility, payment completion and order quality?
new_work: Maintain event definitions, reconciliation rules and checkout test journeys.
Review feedback categories, variant quality and accessibility exceptions.
Investigate assignment imbalance, tracking failures and inconclusive experiments.
Monitor delayed commercial outcomes and maintain restoration procedures.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward choosing audience problems, designing credible tests and coordinating editorial and commercial trade-offs. Preparation becomes faster, while budget, publication and release approvals remain with their existing owners.
reach: Editorial commissioning through evidence-linked content briefs.
Market research through validation of uncertain intent hypotheses.
Interface design through accessible experiment specifications.
Online merchandising through interpretation of order quality and margin.
skills_to_grow: Measurement definitions, source lineage and data quality diagnosis.
Experimental design, statistical uncertainty and causal reasoning.
Multilingual intent research and evaluation of semantic classifications.
Accessible interaction design and checkout economics.
Cross-channel negotiation and clear decision records.
Privacy-aware data use and bounded model evaluation.
role.ambitious_version: Run an audience learning programme that connects search questions, editorial choices and conversion experiments. Expand support to smaller language markets and regional pages, with explicit evidence thresholds and existing approval rights.
